responses.reason: Clearly separates repository exposure policy from routing, authorization and admission controls.
Correctly defines credential handling and excludes credential-bearing inheritance into serving processes.
The revocation barrier is enforceable and accurately describes the limit on recalling in-transit results.

The narrower L2 guarantee is precise, with initial-selection limitations explicit. Optional owner confirmation addresses initial association when required; pending approval must respect the established request deadlines.
Persistent associations, fail-closed recovery and refusal at capacity prevent silent rebinding after rotation, expiry or state loss.
Atomic authorization and admission, synchronized with revocation, resolve the concurrent-binding races.
Identity provenance is an explicit enablement condition, and weaker evidence produces appropriately weaker claims. Identifier reuse is correctly treated as shared binding scope.
Immutable request binding, explicit terminal context, expiry and single-use approval address pairing confusion and replay.
Capability-only operation remains an explicitly weaker mode, without claiming L2 solved or silently downgrading required binding.
The wire check appropriately comes first. Retain the previously agreed IPC, binding lifecycle, concurrency and pairing tests alongside the real-ChatGPT acceptance checks.

summary: Design consensus reached; no critical or major disagreements remain. L1 is capability authorization, L3 is architectural separation, and L2 is prevention of unapproved switching after initial binding, subject to the stated identity and initial-selection limitations. Runtime guarantees remain contingent on the wire check and release acceptance tests. Release 1 stays focused on multi-repository access.
